label: <DEL> step of long sequences, strongest when the first token to recall is 1
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step (94.5% of mass, 93% of activations); it never fires in the copy phase and never when L<=5. The rate and size climb steeply with L (L=9 holds 68% of mass, L=8 28%, L=7 3.5%). Magnitude is set by the first original token, which is the token output at the <DEL> step: first_tok=1 accounts for 62% of mass and all top activations (about 0.85-1.0 of max), and L>=7 with first_tok=1 has precision 0.70. A second tier of first tokens (x,0,q,c,z,f,h,2,y,n) gives weaker firing, mostly at L=9. Other L=9 delimiters fire weakly (lowest quartiles, ~0.01-0.2 of max). A small leftover (5.5% of mass) sits on the last one or two original tokens of L=8/9 sequences that start with 1, at about 0.1-0.4 of max. It does not fire on delimiters of short sequences, even ones starting with 1. The first-token tiering is a lookup set rather than a clean rule, so precision stays limited.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: 1, x, q, 0, z, c; least: w, g, b, d) and the previous input (most: i, r, m, h, o, d; least: n, c, q, 1); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, L=9 & t=9, L=9 & t=8.
